arxiv-1612-07839.title: Poisson measure as a spectral measure of a family of commuting selfadjoint operators, connected with some moment problem
arxiv-1612-07839.creator: Yu. M. Berezansky
arxiv-1612-07839.description: Abstract . It is proved that the Poisson measure is a spectral measure of some family of commuting selfadjoint operators acting on a space constructed from some generalization of the moment problem. \pagespan 311329 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 44A60, 47A57 1.

arxiv-2008-05196.title: RAF-AU Database: In-the-Wild Facial Expressions with Subjective Emotion Judgement and Objective AU Annotations
arxiv-2008-05196.creator: Wen-Jing Yan, Shan Li, Chengtao Que, Jiquan Pei, Weihong Deng
arxiv-2008-05196.description: Abstract Much of the work on automatic facial expression recognition relies on databases containing a certain number of emotion classes and their exaggerated facial configurations (generally six prototypical facial expressions), based on Ekman’s Basic Emotion Theory. However, recent studies have revealed that facial expressions in our human life can be blended with multiple basic emotions.

arxiv-2203-01889.title: Quantum Reinforcement Learning via Policy Iteration
arxiv-2203-01889.creator: El Amine Cherrat, Iordanis Kerenidis, Anupam Prakash
arxiv-2203-01889.description: Abstract Quantum computing has shown the potential to substantially speed up machine learning applications, in particular for supervised and unsupervised learning. Reinforcement learning, on the other hand, has become essential for solving many decision making problems and policy iteration methods remain the foundation of such approaches.

arxiv-2211-16840.title: Holographic Study of the Q ​ Q ¯ Q\bar{Q} Chaotic Dynamics in General Thermal Background
arxiv-2211-16840.creator: \firstname Nicola \lastname Losacco \fnsep
arxiv-2211-16840.description: Abstract The holographic approach is applied to study the chaotic behaviour of a strongly coupled Q ​ Q ¯ Q\bar{Q} pair in general thermal background. We consider two different backgrounds, one with finite temperature and baryon density, and one with finite temperature and constant magnetic field along a fixed direction.

arxiv-2212-01292.title: Novel Data Analysis Tool for the Evaluation of Coincidence Doppler Broadening Spectra of the Positron-Electron Annihilation Line Journal: Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A
arxiv-2212-01292.creator: Leon Chryssos, Christoph Hugenschmidt
arxiv-2212-01292.description: Abstract Coincidence Doppler Broadening Spectroscopy (CDBS) of the 511 keV annihilation line reveals the elemental signature at the annihilation site in matter. For this reason, CDBS enables the analysis of foreign atoms in the host matrix, vacancy-solute complexes and precipitates in solids.

arxiv-2212-08093.title: Global Extinction: Gemini North and South GMOS Combined Photometry Relative to the Gaia Catalog, and Long-Term Atmospheric Change Note: Accepted, August 9, 2026
arxiv-2212-08093.creator: Eric Steinbring
arxiv-2212-08093.description: Abstract Effects of long-term atmospheric change were looked for in photometry employing Gemini North and South twin Multi-Object Spectrograph (GMOS-N and GMOS-S) archival data. The whole GMOS imaging database, beginning from 2003, was compared against the all-sky Gaia object catalog, yielding ∼ 10 6 \sim 10^{6} Sloan r ′ {\rm r}^{\prime} -filter samples, ending in 2021.

arxiv-2405-03999.title: Interaction Design for Human-AI Choreography Co-creation Conference: ; ; CCS: Human-centered computing Interactive systems and tools
arxiv-2405-03999.creator: Yimeng Liu
arxiv-2405-03999.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yimeng Liu. Human-AI co-creation aims to combine human and AI strengths for artistic results exceeding individual capabilities. Frameworks exist for painting, music, and poetry, but choreography’s embodied nature demands a dedicated approach. This paper explores AI-assisted choreography techniques (e.g., generative ideation, embodied improvisation) and analyzes interaction design — how humans and AI collaborate and communicate — to inform the design considerations of future human-AI choreography co-creation systems. 0 0 footnotetext: Licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0).

arxiv-2408-00281.title: The “Galois Correspondence” for n n -Stacks
arxiv-2408-00281.creator: Yuxiang Yao
arxiv-2408-00281.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yuxiang Yao. We prove an essentially surjective Galois-correspondence-like functor for n n -stacks. More specifically, it gives an essentially surjective functor from the ∞ \infty -category of n n -stacks of finite sets with an action of the fundamental group of X X to the ∞ \infty -category of Deligne-Mumford n n -stacks étale over a connected scheme X X . Introduction

In this note, we will introduce an essentially surjective Galois-correspondence-like functor for
n
-stacks.

arxiv-2408-07635.title: Unveiling Stripe-shaped Charge Modulations in Doped Mott Insulators
arxiv-2408-07635.creator: Ning Xia, Yuchen Guo, Shuo Yang
arxiv-2408-07635.description: Abstract Inspired by recent experimental findings, we investigate various scenarios of the doped Hubbard model with impurity potentials. We calculate the lattice Green’s function in a finite-size cluster and then map it to the continuum real space, which allows for a direct comparison with scanning-tunneling-microscopy measurements on the local density of states.

arxiv-2411-15270.title: BanglaEmbed: Efficient Sentence Embedding Models for a Low-Resource Language Using Cross-Lingual Distillation Techniques
arxiv-2411-15270.creator: Muhammad Rafsan Kabir, Md. Mohibur Rahman Nabil, Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Khan
arxiv-2411-15270.description: Abstract Sentence-level embedding is essential for various tasks that require understanding natural language. Many studies have explored such embeddings for high-resource languages like English. However, low-resource languages like Bengali (a language spoken by almost two hundred and thirty million people) are still under-explored.

arxiv-2505-20755.title: Uni-Instruct: One-step Diffusion Model through Unified Diffusion Divergence Instruction
arxiv-2505-20755.creator: Yifei Wang, Weimin Bai, Colin Zhang, Debing Zhang, Weijian Luo, He Sun
arxiv-2505-20755.description: Abstract In this paper, we unify more than 10 existing one-step diffusion distillation approaches, such as Diff-Instruct, DMD, SIM, SiD, f f -distill, etc, inside a theory-driven framework which we name the Uni-Instruct . Uni-Instruct is motivated by our proposed diffusion expansion theory of the f f -divergence family.

arxiv-2507-07170.title: Holomorphic bootstrap for RCFT: signs and bounds for quasi-characters
arxiv-2507-07170.creator: and Sunil Mukhi
arxiv-2507-07170.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by and Sunil Mukhi. Quasi-characters are solutions of simple modular differential equations that form an explicit basis for the space of all admissible characters that can potentially describe rational CFT. They were classified for rank- 2 2 in arXiv:1810.09472 [hep-th], where it was conjectured that their q q -series has coefficients of alternating sign that stabilise to a fixed sign at order c 12 \frac{c}{12} and sometimes undergo more exotic behaviour – where c c is the central charge.

arxiv-2509-26429.title: An Orthogonal Learner for Individualized Outcomes in Markov Decision Processes
arxiv-2509-26429.creator: Emil Javurek, Valentyn Melnychuk, Jonas Schweisthal, Konstantin Hess, Dennis Frauen, Stefan Feuerriegel
arxiv-2509-26429.description: Abstract Predicting individualized potential outcomes in sequential decision-making is central for optimizing therapeutic decisions in personalized medicine (e.g., which dosing sequence to give to a cancer patient). However, predicting potential outcomes over long horizons is notoriously difficult. Existing methods that break the curse of the horizon typically lack strong theoretical guarantees such as orthogonality and quasi-oracle efficiency.

arxiv-2601-08978.title: Collective inhibition of light scattering from atoms into an optical cavity at a magic frequency
arxiv-2601-08978.creator: Á. Kurkó, B. Gábor, D. Varga, A. Simon, T. Barmashova, A. Dombi, T. W. Clark, F. I. B. Williams, D. Nagy, A. Vukics, P. Domokos
arxiv-2601-08978.description: Abstract We report on the observation of a new magic frequency within the hyperfine structure of the D2 line of 87 Rb atoms at which the scattering of light into a high-finesse cavity is suppressed by an interplay between quantum interference and the strong collective coupling of atoms to the cavity.

europmc-pmc3546368.title: Environmental inequality in exposures to airborne particulate matter components in the United States.
europmc-pmc3546368.creator: Bell ML, Ebisu K.
europmc-pmc3546368.description: Background Growing evidence indicates that toxicity of fine particulate matter ≤ 2.5 μm in diameter (PM2.5) differs by chemical component. Exposure to components may differ by population. Objectives We investigated whether exposures to PM2.5 components differ by race/ethnicity,

pages-from-a-journal-with-other-papers.creator: William Hale White

pmc-10710061.title: Bimodular architecture of bacterial effector SAP05 that drives ubiquitin-independent targeted protein degradation
pmc-10710061.creator: Qun Liu, Abbas Maqbool, Federico G. Mirkin, Yeshveer Singh, Clare E. M. Stevenson, David M. Lawson, Sophien Kamoun, Weijie Huang, Saskia A. Hogenhout
pmc-10710061.description: SignificanceThis study reveals the structure–function relationships and mechanisms of SAP05 bacterial effectors in a unique protein degradation process. Crystal structures demonstrate that SAP05 acts as a scaffold, facilitating efficient substrate degradation by bringing together the substrate and the 26S proteasome receptor Rpn10.

pmc-11355203.title: Major Causes of Conflicting Interpretations of Variant Pathogenicity in Rare Disease: A Systematic Analysis
pmc-11355203.creator: Tatyana E Lazareva, Yury A Barbitoff, Yulia A Nasykhova, Andrey S Glotov, Miquéias Lopes-Pacheco
pmc-11355203.description: The identification of the genetic causes of inherited disorders from next-generation sequencing (NGS) data remains a complicated process, in particular due to challenges in interpretation of the vast amount of generated data and hundreds of candidate variants identified. Inconsistencies in variant classification, where genetic centers classify the same variant differently, can hinder accurate diagnoses for rare diseases.

pmc-11635365.title: Long-term efficacy of drug-coated balloon only angioplasty for IgG4-related coronary artery disease: a case report
pmc-11635365.creator: Mayu Yamada, Katsumi Ueno, Yoshinobu Kojima, Mitsuru Watanabe, Norihiko Morita, Claudio Montalto, Andi Rroku, Pok-Tin Tang
pmc-11635365.description: BackgroundAlthough coronary artery involvement in patients with IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is rare, emergency revascularization is recommended for managing acute coronary syndrome. However, coronary aneurysm formation and stent migration after sirolimus-eluting stent implantation have been reported for this disease. Thus, new treatment modalities are warranted for the management of coronary artery disease in this vasculitis.

pmc-12430954.title: Sensor-Oriented Framework for Underwater Acoustic Signal Classification Using EMD–Wavelet Filtering and Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest
pmc-12430954.creator: Sergii Babichev, Oleg Yarema, Yevheniy Khomenko, Denys Senchyshen, Bohdan Durnyak, Jingjing Wang
pmc-12430954.description: Ship acoustic signal classification is essential for vessel identification, underwater navigation, and maritime security. Traditional methods struggle with the non-stationary nature and noise of ship acoustic signals, reducing classification accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose an automated pipeline that integrates Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), adaptive wavelet filtering, feature selection, and a Bayesian-optimized Random Forest classifier.

pmc-12536638.title: The harder the prep, the harder the recovery: a qualitative exploration of physique athlete perspectives on competition weight loss and restoration
pmc-12536638.creator: Claire Buechel, Kate Pumpa, Naroa Etxebarria, Michelle Minehan
pmc-12536638.description: BackgroundThere is growing recognition of Low Energy Availability (LEA) symptoms in physique sports, however there are no clear recovery guidelines. This study explores how athletes perceive and manage recovery from prolonged and intentional LEA. Findings will inform future recovery strategies aimed at restoring energy availability.

pmc-12568808.title: Low skeletal muscle index combined with reduced bone density increases mortality rate in older adults with heart failure
pmc-12568808.creator: Qinyue Wang, Yixiang Ye, Shuxin Zhang, Junchao Yang, Huilin Che, Xinkai Qu, Lin Qi, Mingxuan Li, Kailei Shi
pmc-12568808.description: BackgroundHeart failure (HF) is associated with high mortality and poor prognosis in older adults. Reduced skeletal muscle mass and low bone mineral density are prevalent comorbidities in this population; however, their combined impact on clinical outcomes remains underexplored.AmisThis study aimed to investigate the prognostic impact of reduced skeletal muscle mass and bone mineral density in older adults with HF.

pmc-12656112.title: Research on the Design of Micromixer Based on Acoustic Streaming-Driven Sharp-Edge Structures
pmc-12656112.creator: Kaihao Bai, Heting Qiao, Jixiang Cai, Jinlong Hu, Zhiqi Wang
pmc-12656112.description: This paper presents a three-dimensional, acoustic streaming-driven circular micromixer with sharp-edge structures and the coupling mechanism between acoustic streaming and background flow in biological systems. A piezoelectric transducer induces vibrations in the sharp-edge structures, generating a localized, intense acoustic field that produces a nonlinear acoustic streaming vortex at the tip. The disk-shaped mixing chamber design enhances acoustic field perturbation.

pmc-12817759.title: Evaluation of road infrastructure in Yerevan, Armenia through the lens of pedestrian and child safety: a school-based analysis
pmc-12817759.creator: Emily N Terian, Haig J Minasian, Jefrin Johny, Araksya Gevorgyan, Sharon A Chekijian
pmc-12817759.description: IntroductionTraffic-related injury is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally, especially among children. In Armenia, traffic-related mortality rates are the second highest among European Union and former Soviet countries. Currently, there are no published studies on pedestrian safety in Armenia and no notable examinations of pedestrian safety infrastructure.

pmc-13481933.title: Monte Carlo microdosimetry of 211At in multi-species thyroid follicle models: AlfaMC versus MCNPX and Geant4
pmc-13481933.creator: Arman Romiani, Anders Josefsson, Roumiana Chakarova, Eva Forssell-Aronsson
pmc-13481933.description: BackgroundRadionuclide therapy is an increasingly used treatment modality for patients with disseminated cancer diseases. Tumor-binding radiopharmaceuticals labelled with the alpha-particle emitter astatine-211 (211At) are of interest to enable high radiation absorbed doses to small tumors. The alpha particles emitted by 211At will deposit all their energy in a short-range including neighboring cells, causing localized irradiation.
